children: fell 4.43% premarket after beating on both lines but guiding fourth-quarter revenue to a midpoint below expectations. Third-quarter revenue rose 13% to a record $6.76 billion, compared to a $6.69 billion Wall Street consensus. Non-GAAP earnings came in at $6.13 per share.

GAAP net income was $1.83 billion against $1.77 billion a year earlier, a 3.1% increase, while GAAP earnings per share rose 10.5% to $4.62. The difference is the share count, down to 395 million from 424 million after Adobe repurchased about 9.5 million shares in the quarter. Operating expenses grew 14.8% against 12.9% revenue growth, pulling GAAP operating margin to 34.8% from 36.3%.

The AI numbers are the bull case. AI-first annual recurring revenue grew more than 150% year over year and Adobe passed one billion monthly active users across its creativity and productivity products. Total ARR exiting the quarter was $27.50 billion. Steve Day, signing as interim chief financial officer, pointed to a freemium strategy expanding the user base.

Adobe lifted fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to between $26.576 billion and $26.626 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $24.45 to $24.50. Full-year ARR growth is guided at 10.2%. Fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $6.80 billion to $6.85 billion, a midpoint of $6.825 billion against consensus of $6.85 billion.

title: Adobe Beats on Both Lines But Guides Below Consensus
